papers.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: An Open and Efficient Small Language Model for Fast Conversational Agents
papers.brief: 基于Gemma-4-E4B-it继续后训练，提升工具调用、指令遵循和输入依据对齐，并搭配DFlash推测解码，面向低内存本地助手与边缘设备。
papers.tldr: 这款开放小模型强化多轮工具调用，并以推测解码加速本地对话智能体。
papers.what_it_is: 基于Gemma-4-E4B-it继续后训练，提升工具调用、指令遵循和输入依据对齐，并搭配DFlash推测解码，面向低内存本地助手与边缘设备。
key_points: 21项基准中，相比两款基线平均准确率最高
推理与非推理模式下，输出词元均最少
DFlash在并发1时将单用户解码速度提升至2.74倍
papers.why_notable: 将对话质量、多轮工具使用与低内存推理效率结合，为本地语音助手和嵌入式智能体提供更实用的开放模型选择。
papers.abstract: We introduce Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an open and efficient small language model further post-trained from Gemma-4-E4B-it and optimized for speed and intelligence per GB of memory used for fast conversational agents. The model carries forward Gemma's strong conversational capabilities and further improves multi-turn tool use, instruction following, and input grounding for fast, local voice/device assistants, interactive personas, and embedded/Edge interfaces. The model combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power voice/device assistants, interactive characters and robotic/IoT interfaces running on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. Experiments on 21 benchmarks show that Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB achieves the highest average accuracy while generating the fewest output tokens in both reasoning and non-reasoning modes, compared with Gemma-4-E4B-it and Qwen3.5-4B. The model is released with a DFlash drafter. With DFlash, Bolt E4B achieves $2.74\times$ the per-user decode speed of inference without speculative decoding at concurrency~1, and $1.21\times$ the generation throughput of Gemma-4-E4B-it with MTP at batch size 1.

papers.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
papers.brief: Accelerate Bench构建32项CPU优化任务，让编码智能体在保持计算正确的前提下自主选择优化位置与方法，并通过公开测试和独立验证器评估最终性能。
papers.tldr: 该基准评测智能体对完整程序的加速能力，揭示跨代码与运行配置协同的重要性。
papers.what_it_is: Accelerate Bench构建32项CPU优化任务，让编码智能体在保持计算正确的前提下自主选择优化位置与方法，并通过公开测试和独立验证器评估最终性能。
key_points: 评测16个编码智能体，Score@1为25.5%至67.4%
两支领先智能体在至少22项任务上实现2倍加速
相同源码仅改变构建与运行设置，速度为0.29至2.12倍
papers.why_notable: 它将评测从局部代码改写推进到完整应用优化，区分正确性与实际加速收益，并提供执行轨迹以分析优化过程。
papers.abstract: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. Public testing supports iterative development, and a separate verifier scores the final submission. On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are correct, and the size of the speedup separates them: the two leading agents are at least 2x faster on 22 or more of the 32 tasks, while the other fourteen reach 2x on 8 to 17 and leave 125 of their 412 correct outcomes below 1.25x. Controlled replays show why coordination across an application matters: identical source code runs between 0.29x and 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings, and one code change is worth 1.01x or 6.4x depending on another. Accelerate Bench pairs executable workloads with agents' programs and trajectories to evaluate both their gains and the process behind them.

papers.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
papers.brief: 推出3200亿参数混合专家模型，以专用编码器和投影器接入分子、生物序列及光谱信息，并构建可验证环境培养工具调用、编程与科学实验能力。
papers.tldr: 以科学多模态编码和可验证任务训练，增强大规模模型的证据推理与交互执行能力。
papers.what_it_is: 推出3200亿参数混合专家模型，以专用编码器和投影器接入分子、生物序列及光谱信息，并构建可验证环境培养工具调用、编程与科学实验能力。
key_points: Sci-Perception将科学模态映射至共享骨干
以执行结果、环境状态或产物验证任务完成
覆盖七领域33项基准，五基线比较中四项第一
papers.why_notable: 将科学数据理解与实际任务执行结合，在文档证据利用、可验证表格产出和机器学习实验上表现突出，拓展科学智能体的应用路径。
papers.abstract: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space of a shared backbone, which processes them alongside text and images. To develop the model's agent capabilities, we construct verifiable environments for tool use, search, and coding, as well as specialized workflows involving machine learning experiments and scientific software. Task completion is checked against execution results, changes in environment state, or submitted artifacts. We evaluate Sage S1.5 Flash on 33 benchmarks across seven domains. In the primary comparison against five baselines, it ranks first on OfficeQA Pro (72.2), MLE-bench Lite (90.3 HumanRank), Harvey LAB, and SpreadsheetBench~2, and second on OSWorld-Verified (85.2), WebArena-Verified (67.6), and DeepResearch Bench~II (54.2). These results show particular strengths in using documentary evidence, producing verifiable workbooks, and carrying out machine learning tasks, alongside competitive performance in desktop and browser workflows that require the model to act on visual feedback.

papers.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
papers.brief: 推出覆盖0.9B稠密模型至375B-A23B混合专家模型的六款模型，以注意力结构改进增强推理、扩散适配器加速解码，并开放数据与开发全流程。
papers.tldr: 六款全开源模型兼顾推理与智能体任务，并公开训练全流程以支持复现。
papers.what_it_is: 推出覆盖0.9B稠密模型至375B-A23B混合专家模型的六款模型，以注意力结构改进增强推理、扩散适配器加速解码，并开放数据与开发全流程。
key_points: MoVA与softplus门控使4B激活参数逼近32B稠密模型
Uno无损扩散适配器无需草稿模型，解码最高提速2.2倍
公开约10T合成预训练词元及生成流水线
papers.why_notable: 开放范围延伸到中间检查点与数据构建流水线；四款模型共享22T词元语料和配方，为规模与稀疏性的受控研究提供基础。
papers.abstract: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/

papers.title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
papers.brief: JEPA4R用单深度相机点云学习世界模型，在潜空间预测和规划，并以冻结表征训练策略头。通过解码未来点云，可直观看到模型预测的几何演化。
papers.tldr: 以点云潜空间预测与规划驱动机器人操作，并实现数字孪生到真机零样本迁移。
papers.what_it_is: JEPA4R用单深度相机点云学习世界模型，在潜空间预测和规划，并以冻结表征训练策略头。通过解码未来点云，可直观看到模型预测的几何演化。
key_points: 冻结模型解码200步点云，平均点误差不超过1.1厘米
MetaWorld与Adroit Relocate得分98.4%和88.0%
仅在数字孪生训练，零样本部署至夹爪与灵巧手
papers.why_notable: 将操作所需的度量几何显式纳入世界模型，并让长期预测可视化；多基准领先与真机迁移结果增强了其机器人应用价值。
papers.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

papers.title: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
papers.brief: SilentGuard在工具调用执行框架中，用正确接口应满足的不变量检验返回结果，并阻断违规数值。它通过拒答避免错误，而非依赖模型警告或修复接口。
papers.tldr: 将接口结果校验与拦截交给执行框架，显著减少智能体采信静默错误
papers.what_it_is: SilentGuard在工具调用执行框架中，用正确接口应满足的不变量检验返回结果，并阻断违规数值。它通过拒答避免错误，而非依赖模型警告或修复接口。
key_points: 15个公共研究API中11个存在静默故障，计数最多虚增691倍
7个开放模型错误率从74.0%降至1.7%
同一检查仅发警告仍有70.1%错误，强制拦截才有效
papers.why_notable: 把可靠性控制从模型判断转为执行层约束，在无故障任务上不损失表现；对新故障也能降低错误，但主要靠拒答而非恢复。
papers.abstract: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. It tests each result against invariants that any correct API must satisfy and withholds values that break one. We find silent failures in 11 of 15 public research APIs, with counts inflated up to 691 times. Current fixes leave over 70% of answers wrong, and agents report 77.4% of counts a judge flags. Across 7 open models, SilentGuard cuts wrong answers on its target faults from 74.0% to 1.7%, with no loss on fault-free tasks. On three frontier models they fall from 70.2% to 0.5%. A warning from the same check leaves 70.1% wrong, so enforcement is the key. On new fault types, the harness alone cuts wrong answers from 61.1% to 24.5%. It avoids wrong answers by abstaining rather than recovering.

papers.title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
papers.brief: Turing Agent协调定理与证明形式化智能体，完成研究级数学的端到端验证。核心结合结构化证明分解、并行验证、经验积累与选择性语义审查。
papers.tldr: 通过分层智能体协作，将研究级数学证明转化为机器验证的可信知识。
papers.what_it_is: Turing Agent协调定理与证明形式化智能体，完成研究级数学的端到端验证。核心结合结构化证明分解、并行验证、经验积累与选择性语义审查。
key_points: Formal TCS Bench忠实形式化成功率约57–62%
TCS版RLMEval子集整体pass@1达83%
完成3项此前未解决任务，其中一项需约百条辅助断言
papers.why_notable: 价值不止于检查证明正确性，还在于忠实保留原命题语义；验证过程可发现更简洁的证明、移除多余依赖，并积累可复用知识。
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing mathematical discovery, moving beyond benchmark-level problem solving to tackle frontier research problems. This progress is ushering mathematics into an era of proof abundance, raising a fundamental challenge: how can we ensure the correctness of the ever-growing volume of AI-generated proofs and transform them into trustworthy, machine-verified mathematical knowledge? We introduce Turing Agent, an agent harness designed to orchestrate end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics. Its wo-scale architecture integrates theorem formalization and proof formalization agents, empowered by structured proof decomposition, parallel verification, accumulated proof experience, and selective semantic review. Leveraging our collaborations with theoretical computer science (TCS) researchers, we focus our evaluation on TCS, a particularly demanding domain characterized by intricate quantification, complex dependencies, and stringent semantic requirements. Against direct generation and general-purpose coding harnesses, including Codex CLI and Claude Code, Turing Agent achieves approximately 57-62% faithful formalization success on Formal TCS Bench and 83% overall pass@1 on a TCS-focused subset of RLMEval, using GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Notably, Turing Agent, built on DeepSeek, successfully completes the formal verification of three previously unresolved TCS tasks from OpenAI's October 2026 collection. One particularly challenging TCS problem required about a hundred formally verified auxiliary claims. Moreover, by actively exploring and refining the formalization process, Turing Agent can uncover simpler alternative proofs, expose unnecessary dependencies in original proofs, and generate reusable mathematical knowledge as a byproduct of verification.

papers.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
papers.brief: RepoFactory将真实仓库转为可验证的从零构建项目环境，再通过环境演化循环，以有效性、结构耦合和实现范围的乘积目标优化训练价值。
papers.tldr: 用代理反馈迭代优化仓库训练环境，规模化提升长程编程智能体能力。
papers.what_it_is: RepoFactory将真实仓库转为可验证的从零构建项目环境，再通过环境演化循环，以有效性、结构耦合和实现范围的乘积目标优化训练价值。
key_points: RepoFactory生成10,159个环境，覆盖17个软件领域
环境演化循环以代理反馈优化三项指标的乘积
NL2Repo-Bench提升22.6个百分点，无演化时为17.5
papers.why_notable: 把环境验证推进到训练价值优化，用及时代理反馈减少对昂贵模型评估的依赖；五项基准平均增益由6.4升至8.5个百分点。
papers.abstract: Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) often requires model rollouts or model training followed by downstream evaluation, with costs and feedback delays amplified on long-horizon tasks. How can we use timely, reliable proxy signals to improve training value and synthesize environments at scale? We present RepoFactory, an automated pipeline that converts real repositories into verifiable environments where agents build complete projects from scratch given a language specification. Its Environment Evolution Loop optimizes a multiplicative objective combining validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope through proxy feedback. RepoFactory produces 10,159 environments across 17 software domains. Training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on these environments yields RepoHorizen-35B-A3B, which achieves gains of 22.6 percentage points on NL2Repo-Bench and 8.5 points on average across five benchmarks covering long-horizon coding and agentic tasks in real-world production settings, compared with 17.5 and 6.4 points without environment evolution. These results highlight the training value of RepoFactory environments and the additional gains from the Environment Evolution Loop.

papers.title: Instant Weight-Space Consolidation for Long-Term Memory in LLMs
papers.brief: CLAM用循环超网络将会话激活整合为低秩适配器，无需梯度更新或语言模型生成。固定大小的门控潜状态跨会话积累知识，情景缓冲区补充原文细节。
papers.tldr: CLAM以单次前向传播将跨会话经验写入适配器，实现高效长期记忆。
papers.what_it_is: CLAM用循环超网络将会话激活整合为低秩适配器，无需梯度更新或语言模型生成。固定大小的门控潜状态跨会话积累知识，情景缓冲区补充原文细节。
key_points: LoCoMo与LongMemEval-S上测试三个2–7B模型
领先智能体记忆基线1–45点，建库提速3–151倍
缓冲区缺失证据时，适配器增益12–15个准确率点
papers.why_notable: 把长期记忆从外部文本检索推进到模型参数整合，同时避免在线反向传播；双通道设计兼顾跨会话知识积累与细节保真。
papers.abstract: Agentic memory systems give LLMs persistent memory by extracting experience into text and retrieving it at query time, but the model itself does not evolve: however many interactions it has had, it starts each query the same. Extraction errors compound, implicit cross-session patterns that no single fragment states cannot be surfaced, and the construction cost grows with every conversation. Fine-tuning on past interactions does change the weights, but requires backpropagation at serving time and degrades on long histories. We introduce CLAM (Carried Latent Adapter Memory), which combines the strengths of both: a recurrent hypernetwork performs parametric consolidation, compiling a stream of session activations into a low-rank adapter in a single forward pass with no gradient steps and no language-model generation calls, while a complementary episodic buffer supplies verbatim detail at inference. A gated latent state carries knowledge across sessions in fixed size, so the parametric memory accumulates without growing. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S across three open models (2-7B parameters), CLAM leads all agentic baselines by 1-45 points and all gradient-based parametric methods by 10-45 points, while requiring zero generative LLM calls, zero gradient steps, and 3-151x less wall-clock time than extraction systems to build its memory. The two channels are complementary: the consolidated adapter adds 12-15 accuracy points when the episodic buffer misses the gold evidence, and still adds 4-5 points even with an oracle buffer.

papers.title: Inside the Trading Loop: Markets, Models, and Moves with LLM Agents
papers.brief: 构建混合多智能体交易系统，由新闻与宏观智能体提交结构化报告，协调器配置股票权重和现金。组合采用动量策略与规则执行，并以模拟账户和历史回放评估。
papers.tldr: 融合大模型分析与规则交易的多智能体系统取得较高模拟收益，但回撤更大。
papers.what_it_is: 构建混合多智能体交易系统，由新闻与宏观智能体提交结构化报告，协调器配置股票权重和现金。组合采用动量策略与规则执行，并以模拟账户和历史回放评估。
key_points: 券商模拟账户收益34.5%，同期SPY为14.4%
启用确定性回退的账户最大回撤高于SPY
固定现金配置收益接近立场驱动配置；短报告改善解析
papers.why_notable: 将语言模型研判接入完整交易闭环，并区分模拟账户与模型配置回放结果；收益与回撤的对照有助于检验实际配置价值。
papers.abstract: We built a hybrid multi-agent trading system that combines large language model (LLM) analysts with momentum-based portfolio construction and rule-based execution. Company-news and macroeconomic agents return structured reports to a coordinator that sets stock weights and cash reserves. We evaluate the portfolio engine using its broker-recorded paper account, which operated with deterministic fallbacks, and compare LLM-enabled configurations through retrospective replays. From March 11 to August 28, 2026, the account returned 34.5%, compared with 14.4% for the S&P 500 fund SPY over the same dates. This raw return advantage came with a larger maximum drawdown. Reconstructed policies also finish above matched SPY and QQQ references when assessments are used in the same session or deferred to the next. Design comparisons examine cash authority, selective invocation, and response contracts. A constant-cash control gives a return estimate close to stance-based sizing, and shorter report contracts improve observed parsing but can change recommendations.

papers.title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
papers.brief: SWE-CoWork将编码智能体置于模拟工程组织，从简短交接出发，向同事和工作记录获取需求、处理冲突并实现改动，最终用私有可执行测试评估交付。
papers.tldr: 组织协作基准揭示，编码智能体能通过部分测试，却难以完整交付任务。
papers.what_it_is: SWE-CoWork将编码智能体置于模拟工程组织，从简短交接出发，向同事和工作记录获取需求、处理冲突并实现改动，最终用私有可执行测试评估交付。
key_points: 101项任务覆盖101个真实仓库、11种语言
每项任务配置26名职责与知识受限的模拟同事
领先模型通过约63%的F2P测试，完整交付率不足8%
papers.why_notable: 它把评测从代码实现扩展到组织内的需求追踪与交付；预先提供完整需求仍未提升任务成功率，说明瓶颈不止信息获取。
papers.abstract: A coding agent working within a software organization must establish what to build, collaborate with colleagues, and verify what it delivers. We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct responsibilities, bounded knowledge, and controlled collaboration behavior. Starting from a brief handoff, agents must recover requirements distributed across colleagues and workplace records, reconcile conflicting evidence, and implement changes evaluated by private executable tests. We evaluate eleven models and find a substantial gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery. The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments. Providing complete requirements upfront improves F2P by approximately 16 percentage points for Seed Evolving and GPT-6 Astra, yet leaves complete task success unchanged. Requirement-level trajectory analysis reveals failures throughout the delivery process: Claude-Opus-5.5 directs a mean of 93% of first questions about queried cards to their accountable owners across runs but obtains only 64% of colleague-held requirements. Deferred questions go unfollowed, implementations remain incomplete even after requirements are acquired, and 31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests. These findings highlight sustained requirement tracking, from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, as a key challenge for reliable autonomous software engineering.

papers.title: SWE-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Coding
papers.brief: 研究将大模型的编码智能体能力蒸馏给小模型：学生在可执行代码仓库中交互，教师监督学生访问的轨迹前缀，并探索缓存教师评分的离线与跨分词器方案。
papers.tldr: 用学生自身轨迹蒸馏编码智能体，提升修复能力并显著降低训练成本
papers.what_it_is: 研究将大模型的编码智能体能力蒸馏给小模型：学生在可执行代码仓库中交互，教师监督学生访问的轨迹前缀，并探索缓存教师评分的离线与跨分词器方案。
key_points: OPD使Qwen3.5-9B的Pro解决率从35.9%升至39.4%
离线缓存教师评分，GPU时数减少59.4%—72.6%
top-K反向KL损失下降仍可能伴随严重重复
papers.why_notable: 表明学生轨迹监督可迁移长程编码能力，离线蒸馏也能兼顾成本与效果；同时揭示训练损失下降不等于智能体表现改善。
papers.abstract: In this work, we study on-policy distillation (OPD) for transferring agentic coding capabilities from a large teacher model to a smaller student model. Prior work has focused primarily on reasoning and short-horizon agentic tasks. We present SWE-OPD, a minimal OPD study for software engineering, where the student interacts with executable repositories and the teacher supervises the prefixes visited by the student. Across three teacher--student pairs, two training sources, and three SWE benchmarks, we find that on-policy supervision transfers coding capability: supervision from Qwen3.6-27B increases the SWE-bench Pro resolve rate of Qwen3.5-9B from 35.9% to 39.4%. Refreshing trajectories is not strictly required either, as an offline variant with cached teacher scores still improves over the student baselines while cutting end-to-end GPU-hours by 59.4%--72.6% and halving peak GPU allocation, at benchmark-dependent accuracy. Furthermore, we extend the offline variant to corss-tokenizer scenarios: distilling GLM-4.5-Air from DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 raises its SWE-bench Pro and Multilingual resolve rate from 35.8% to 39.7% and from 41.8% to 46.2%, around 4% and 4.6% improvement, respectively. We also find that a decreasing loss, however, does not necessarily indicate improved agent performance: under top-$K$ reverse-KL loss, one student exhibits severe repetition despite a decreasing loss. We identify a support-mass gradient term as a potential mechanism underlying this failure.

papers.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
papers.brief: 推出医疗AI评测框架，以三类医疗角色和三种能力组织基准，经审计与复现筛选公开测试，并加入私有诊断推理测试，汇总总分及分项表现。
papers.tldr: 以角色与能力双维度评测医疗大模型，揭示综合排名掩盖的场景差异。
papers.what_it_is: 推出医疗AI评测框架，以三类医疗角色和三种能力组织基准，经审计与复现筛选公开测试，并加入私有诊断推理测试，汇总总分及分项表现。
key_points: 388个候选经审计与独立复现，选出4个公开基准
加入InclusionMed-DxFiles，共覆盖九格中的三格
前十模型均在患者沟通上优于临床决策
papers.why_notable: 模型综合分仅为17.5至49.1分，排名随角色与能力变化，近似分数的推理成本也有差异，为按医疗场景选型提供依据。
papers.abstract: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the InclusionMed Index, with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100. The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, showing that a model's rank varied with the role or capability considered. A within-benchmark analysis using task-level tags showed that the ten highest-ranked models in the Index all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making. Models with similar Index scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost. These findings highlight the need for evaluation covering more diverse healthcare needs and for context-specific model selection. Through open collaboration and community contributions, InclusionMed seeks to ensure that diverse healthcare needs worldwide shape how medical AI progress is defined and measured.

papers.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
papers.brief: SPILLWAY将动作目标准入与文本清洗解耦：依据工具类型字段和固定委托规则确定放行目标，再清除匹配规则的指令文本，无需逐任务规划。
papers.tldr: 以确定性目标准入与文本清洗分离，低开销阻止工具智能体被注入重定向。
papers.what_it_is: SPILLWAY将动作目标准入与文本清洗解耦：依据工具类型字段和固定委托规则确定放行目标，再清除匹配规则的指令文本，无需逐任务规划。
key_points: 目标须来自只读工具的类型字段或固定委托规则
清洗保留删除证据，局部裁判不得恢复涉及该文本目标的调用
覆盖3种骨干；强化学习攻击者平均成功率为0.005
papers.why_notable: 把动作去向的最终约束移出语言模型，形成可审计的拒绝底线；标准模板攻击未能重定向，且几乎不增加模型调用。
papers.abstract: Tool-using agents act on email, files, and payments, so an instruction hidden in a web page or a shared document can make an agent send data or money to an attacker. Many runtime defenses put a language model on the decision that lets an action through, so the decision depends on a model that may read the attacker's text and adds model calls to every step. Provenance defenses keep the model off the final check but need a model to plan or route each task first. Where an action goes can instead be read from the tools' typed returns: an email's sender or a payment's account arrives in a typed field, while injected instructions arrive as free text. SPILLWAY turns this observation into a deterministic floor with no per-task plan. The check admits a call when each target value that appears in tool output but not in the user's task was returned by a read-only tool in a typed field or is covered by a fixed delegation rule. A deterministic sanitizer removes instruction-like regions its fixed rules match before the model reads them and retains the removed spans as evidence, and a local judge may restore a refused call, never one whose target lies in the removed text. Across three backbones, and seven task suites on one of them, no standard templated injection redirects an action to an attacker's target under SPILLWAY, at the highest observed mean utility and composite scores (NRP, ERS) of the defenses we run under that attack. A forged chat template also produces a raw zero, and mean in-scope attack success under a released reinforcement-learning attacker is .005. SPILLWAY reaches this floor with no defense-triggered backbone re-run and almost no added model call. As personal AI agents act on users' email, files, and payments, SPILLWAY gives them an auditable refusal floor on where their actions go that keeps them useful and holds across backbones.

papers.title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
papers.brief: AllocFlow从原始多资产行情直接生成联合仓位，用跨资产流Transformer建模持仓依赖；先模仿策略形成候选组合，再以组合级奖励强化学习。
papers.tldr: 用流匹配直接生成多资产联合仓位，再以强化学习提升收益与回撤表现。
papers.what_it_is: AllocFlow从原始多资产行情直接生成联合仓位，用跨资产流Transformer建模持仓依赖；先模仿策略形成候选组合，再以组合级奖励强化学习。
key_points: 跨资产流Transformer联合生成连续、有正负方向的仓位权重
策略监督模仿后，以冻结策略参照进行组相对强化学习
小时级加密永续合约上，年化净收益由27.79%升至51.38%
papers.why_notable: 将预测、配置与交易目标统一到端到端学习中；无需重训，在额外六个月的2026年未见数据上取得4.90的Calmar比率。
papers.abstract: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from $27.79\%$ to $51.38\%$ and its Calmar ratio from $0.955$ to $4.043$, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of $4.90$ on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.

papers.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
papers.brief: 提出连接流式微调、长程蒸馏与推理的视频生成框架，以分窗去噪建立基础模型，再用长程自生成轨迹训练少步生成器，并压缩历史缓存。
papers.tldr: 通过分窗训练、缓存压缩与长程蒸馏，实现超出训练时长的稳定视频生成。
papers.what_it_is: 提出连接流式微调、长程蒸馏与推理的视频生成框架，以分窗去噪建立基础模型，再用长程自生成轨迹训练少步生成器，并压缩历史缓存。
key_points: WinTF结合窗内双向注意力与历史因果访问
HieraKV分层保留历史，缓存内存最多减少78%
CuLT-DMD固定参数完成长轨迹后，平均局部梯度更新
papers.why_notable: 仅用最长15秒视频训练，基础模型在30秒仍具竞争力；蒸馏模型在HeliosBench最长60秒评测中总分领先。
papers.abstract: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

papers.title: VoxMel TTS Technical Report
papers.brief: 提出无分词器语音合成框架，用固定可逆的双轴Haar变换拆分梅尔谱。语言模型与流匹配头自回归生成粗粒度谱，再以非自回归模块补齐时频残差。
papers.tldr: 通过可逆梅尔分解实现无分词器自回归语音合成，兼顾生成稳定性与细节保真。
papers.what_it_is: 提出无分词器语音合成框架，用固定可逆的双轴Haar变换拆分梅尔谱。语言模型与流匹配头自回归生成粗粒度谱，再以非自回归模块补齐时频残差。
key_points: 双轴Haar分解时频细节，残差不回流自回归历史
0.6B模型训练于10万小时Emilia语音
GRPO后英文WER为1.15%，中文CER为1.17%
papers.why_notable: 绕开学习式声学编码器，提供直接建模梅尔谱的可行路径；四步流头蒸馏接近监督模型的识别错误率，为降低生成开销提供依据。
papers.abstract: Continuous autoregressive TTS relies on an acoustic target that enables stable next-latent modeling while preserving fine-grained acoustic details. While existing approaches employ learned compressed representations (e.g., continuous VAE latents) to render prediction tractable, they rely on complex neural encoders that often cap generation fidelity. Conversely, training-free targets like mel-spectrograms eliminate encoder overhead, yet their potential for autoregressive generation remains largely underexplored. In this work, we propose VoxMel, a tokenizer-free framework for autoregressive TTS that makes stable mel modeling tractable through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform. The transform first decomposes each mel spectrogram along frequency into local averages and a frequency residual, then splits the averaged component along time into Coarse-Mel and a temporal residual. A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head autoregressively generates Coarse-Mel. Non-autoregressive residual tiers then predict the temporal residual from Coarse-Mel, followed by the frequency residual conditioned on the reconstructed Frequency-Averaged Mel. Neither residual is fed back into the autoregressive history. Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model obtains 1.51\% WER and 0.738 speaker similarity (SIM) on test-en, and 1.29\% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh. GRPO improves these results to 1.15\% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17\% CER / 0.776 SIM, respectively. We also distill the guided flow head into two- and four-step students, requiring 2 or 4 head evaluations per coarse frame. The four-step student retains competitive SIM and nearly matches the supervised model in WER/CER.

papers.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
papers.brief: ScaleVLA将5520亿参数的DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash连接可训练动作DiT，并在统一训练设置下比较不同规模骨干对机器人策略的影响。
papers.tldr: 将超大视觉语言骨干接入动作模型，提升机器人少样本学习、泛化与精细操作。
papers.what_it_is: ScaleVLA将5520亿参数的DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash连接可训练动作DiT，并在统一训练设置下比较不同规模骨干对机器人策略的影响。
key_points: 10次示范成功率87.8%，超越2B骨干用50次示范
LIBERO-PRO成功率45.1%，小骨干最高31.3%
真实充电器插接成功率从4/10升至9/10
papers.why_notable: 结果表明超大视觉语言模型的表征可直接增强机器人策略，而不只用于推理；每动作块中位延迟216毫秒，也展示了部署潜力。
papers.abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

papers.title: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier
papers.brief: 研究将每个词元的顶层状态反馈到下一词元输入，并与把同等算力用于更多轮训练的标准Transformer比较，跨模型规模、独立数据量和训练轮数检验收益。
papers.tldr: 潜在反馈在等算力比较中提升训练效率，最多节省近半算力与独立数据。
papers.what_it_is: 研究将每个词元的顶层状态反馈到下一词元输入，并与把同等算力用于更多轮训练的标准Transformer比较，跨模型规模、独立数据量和训练轮数检验收益。
key_points: 潜在反馈最多节省48%算力、47%独立数据
统一缩放律将潜在反馈等效为更多参数的Transformer
60M至271M拟合，778M损失预测误差不超0.3%
papers.why_notable: 它为数据受限时如何分配训练算力提供了直接证据：反馈比单纯重复训练更有效，且收益随每参数独立数据量和重复次数增加。
papers.abstract: When high-quality data runs out, a common practice is to train on it for several epochs, but each repeat is worth less than the last. Latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, is another way to spend that compute, yet it has not been tested against a vanilla Transformer that spends the same compute on more epochs. We run this test across a ladder of model sizes, unique data and epochs, tuning both models at every size and amount of unique data. Latent feedback makes every FLOP and every token count for more except when unique data is scarce relative to model size, a regime that today's models are far from. We find that latent feedback serves as an amplifier: with unique data fixed, it reaches a Transformer's loss with less compute; with epochs fixed, it reaches that loss with less unique data. Furthermore, both savings grow with unique data per parameter and with repetition, and downstream tasks agree. To go beyond our grid, we fit one scaling law to both models, in which latent feedback enters as a Transformer with more parameters; it predicts that both savings keep growing with unique data and repetition. Fitted on models from 60M to 271M parameters, the law predicts the losses at a held-out 778M size to within 0.3% and the gap between the two models to within 0.05%. At most, latent feedback saves 48% of the compute and 47% of the unique data. When data, not compute, is the limit, latent feedback is the better use of a FLOP for a model of a given size.

papers.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
papers.brief: SALA利用未配对人类与机器人视频的语言描述构建语义软邻域，对齐潜在动作，并以机器人动作重建约束控制语义，形成统一的策略监督。
papers.tldr: 通过语义对齐人机潜在动作，让人类视频同时助力机器人预训练与后训练。
papers.what_it_is: SALA利用未配对人类与机器人视频的语言描述构建语义软邻域，对齐潜在动作，并以机器人动作重建约束控制语义，形成统一的策略监督。
key_points: 语言相似度构建软邻域，无需人机配对数据
机器人动作重建将共享潜在空间锚定到控制
人类视频扩量改善预训练误差与后训练成功率
papers.why_notable: 将人类视频从视觉重建素材转为可迁移的动作监督，为减少昂贵机器人数据依赖提供路径，并展示预训练与后训练两轴扩展收益。
papers.abstract: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

papers.title: Re-Reading Is Not Free: Token Traces and Cache-Aware Energy Estimation for LLM Agents in Software Engineering
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from conversational assistants into autonomous agents embedded in software development workflows, estimating their environmental footprint requires moving beyond conventional token-based accounting. Existing energy estimators focus on isolated request-response interactions, overlooking the repeated processing of accumulated context, cache reuse, and work delegated to subagents. We analyze nearly one billion tokens collected across 42 sessions and 752 task episodes over ten weeks of real-world AI-assisted software development. Cached-context reads make up 94.8% of all API-reported tokens, while uncached input accounts for only 0.017%; for every generated token, approximately 260 cached tokens are read. Context grows 5.3-fold over a session compared with 1.4-fold within individual tasks. To quantify the energy implications, we extend an existing analytical inference-energy model to account for cached-context processing, yielding a cache-aware hybrid estimator. It estimates approximately 250 kWh for the workload, compared with approximately 10 kWh from the output-based estimator EcoLogits, a 25-fold difference largely driven by cached-context reads. Neither estimator has been validated on long cached contexts, but no modeling assumption we varied closes the gap. Starting each task from a fresh context would lower our estimate by about 60%. We also find that parent-session logs report only a subagent's final internal call, undercounting delegated tokens by a factor of ten; for this workload the correction changes the energy estimate by about 5%, but token-volume studies are fully exposed to it. Our findings expose a substantial gap between how current energy estimators and agentic workloads treat context, highlighting the need for workflow-level energy accounting that captures context accumulation, cache reuse, and delegated execution.

papers.title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
papers.abstract: Building agentic applications requires combining large language model (LLM) operations, workflow structure and application state, and model-guided routing. With SDKs and agent frameworks, developers connect these components through supporting code that prepares model inputs, propagates state, and dispatches model-selected steps. Workflow changes can require coordinated updates to this code, increasing development and testing effort. Splitting execution logic between application code and framework internals also limits compiler visibility into control flow and state dependencies, hindering automatic optimization. We introduce Agent-Native Programming, which unifies these three components with shared execution semantics. We realize this approach in Jac, a Python-superset language, through "by llm()" for typed model operations and tool use, Object-Spatial Programming for workflow structure and state, and "visit ... by llm()" for model-guided routing. The routing construct derives the model's choices from executable workflow steps and schedules the selected steps. This explicit connection between model decisions and program execution gives the compiler and runtime a common basis for dependency analysis and automatic optimization. Across five benchmarks and five baselines, Jac achieves a 1.8-8.7x reduction in AI-integration code relative to the OpenAI SDK, with competitive observed task quality and lower coding-agent development effort. Two case studies demonstrate speculative execution and service partitioning through configuration alone, using program analysis and runtime checks to preserve workflow behavior under stated conditions.

papers.title: Multi-LLM Agentic AI at the Edge: Joint Agent Scheduling and Resource Allocation
papers.abstract: In this paper, an edge-enabled multi-large language model (LLM) agentic AI architecture is proposed, where one supervisor AI agent and multiple worker AI agents cooperatively execute users' requests at the edge. The supervisor AI agent decouples the user request into a series of sub-tasks and dynamically dispatches them to LLM-equipped worker AI agents via two agentic workflows, i.e., parallel and serial workflows, with a two-level retry mechanism to enhance execution reliability. To prolong the service duration of worker AI agents, the energy minimization problems are formulated by jointly considering AI agent selection and resource allocation, subject to task execution latency and quality of service (QoS) constraints. A resource allocation scheme based on alternating optimization (AO) is proposed. Specifically, for the parallel workflow, the scheme decouples the original problem into bandwidth allocation, retrieval selection and AI agent selection sub-problems, which are iteratively solved by the proposed successive convex approximation (SCA), Lagrangian relaxation (LR), and Gale-Shapley (GS) or LLM-based algorithms, respectively. For the serial workflow, the problem is similarly decoupled into service time allocation, retrieval selection and AI agent selection sub-problems; the optimal service time allocation is obtained via Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, while the latter two sub-problems are addressed by extending the proposed algorithms to the serial scenario. Simulation results show that the proposed resource allocation scheme can reduce system energy consumption compared with other benchmarks, while experiments on a multi-LLM agentic AI system based on Qwen and Llama demonstrate improved task execution success rates.

papers.title: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Cyber-Physical Resilience in Electrical Power and Energy Systems
papers.abstract: Electrical Power and Energy Systems face hybrid threats that combine cyber intrusions, physical sabotage and climate-driven stress, and routinely outpace today's siloed monitoring stacks. We present RESILAGENT, a concept architecture organised around three operational pillars, Sensing & Data Intelligence, Resilience Analytics & Reporting, and Incident Response & Recovery, mediated by a Cloud-based Orchestrator and exercised through a closed Detect-Simulate-Decide-Sign loop. The framework fuses agentic artificial intelligence and multimodal large language models for cross-modal detection, real-time digital twins for what-if simulation, and a permissioned blockchain anchor for tamper-evident threat intelligence and CER/NIS2-aligned evidence. We instantiate it on two scenarios, a transmission operator under coordinated cyber compromise, sabotage and heatwave, and a distribution operator under a supply-chain compromise during a storm, and report an IEEE-bus micro-benchmark that quantifies each pillar through false-data-injection attack detection, cyber-physical fusion lift, N-1 contingency screening and anchor cost.

papers.title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. However, current methods primarily depend on single-pass chain-of-thought reasoning that overlooks brief or localized artifacts, or on predefined multi-agent workflows that offer limited flexibility in selecting relevant inspections. Even with adaptive investigation, optimizing the investigation policy alone does not directly improve the forensic capabilities of fixed experts. We introduce WeVisForensics, an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues. The investigator learns which artifact type to examine, over which window, and when to conclude, and these interactions provide shared feedback for both levels of agents. Our dual-timescale policy optimization strategy, DTPO, closes this loop through fast reinforcement learning of the investigator and slower refinement of the inspectors, guided by annotated artifact intervals, to report subtle artifacts they once dismissed. Furthermore, we curate ForenCue-30K, combining role-specific forensic annotations and interaction trajectories to supervise individual inspections and their coordination, with an accompanying reinforcement-learning pool. Experiments show that WeVisForensics averages 95.2% detection accuracy across in-domain, out-of-domain and agentic benchmarks, 9.0% above the strongest prior detector, while grounding its verdicts in localized evidence.

papers.title: Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential route to automating scientific programming, but their usefulness depends on consistently producing numerically correct code. We extend FEM-Bench to 17 finite element tasks involving nonlinear and history-dependent mechanics and structural dynamics, and evaluate 15 models on implementation and test generation without execution feedback. The best model succeeds in 87.1% of single-pass implementation trials, but rankings differ between tracks. The leading implementer achieves 49.9% joint test success, while the leading tester reaches 82.6%. For six models, we compare single-pass generation with two agentic harnesses that allow code execution and revision. Agentic execution solves some tasks that never succeeded in single-pass trials and improves consistency on others, but gains vary across models and harnesses, and regressions also occur. Claude Opus 5 with SimpleAgent reaches 96.5% Pass@3, the probability of at least one success in three attempts, but 77.1% Pass$^3$, the probability that all three succeed. No model-harness combination exceeds 78.8% Pass$^3$. To understand why agents submit incorrect code after passing their own checks, we analyze 249 failed agentic trajectories and identify six categories of self-verification failure. The most common are inadequate test coverage (73.1%) and reliance on generic consistency checks (70.3%), and in 28.5% of cases the tests share an error with the implementation. Motivated by these findings, an exploratory configuration with separate coder and tester agents achieves the highest observed scores, with 97.6% Pass@3 and 88.8% Pass$^3$. These results identify consistency across attempts and independent verification as the main obstacles to trusting LLM-generated scientific code.

papers.title: Linglong Agent Service: A Runtime for Centralized Agent Reasoning and Distributed Execution
papers.abstract: LLM agents can use remote tools and cloud sandboxes, but integrating reasoning, session state, and heterogeneous execution sites remains a runtime design problem. We present Linglong Agent Service (agentsvc), a self-hosted HTTP service and embeddable Python runtime that treats execution site as a configurable dimension alongside model, tools, and context. A parent service retains inference orchestration, tool descriptions, and conversation history; each inference request selects one child environment for file, shell, terminal, and MCP operations. Direct HTTP and child-initiated WebSocket tunnels carry the same application interfaces, including portable request context and centrally managed updates. The normal core path requires no third-party Python packages, with an optional Windows pseudo-terminal dependency. We further present online_debugger as the process-scale special case of execution-site separation: an instrumented program submits exception evidence, executes session-scoped inspection tools inside the incident process, and resumes the same diagnostic session. Its default prompt requires failing-then-passing reproduction evidence for source changes, while runtime patch activation and failed-call recovery remain unimplemented. We explain the design through constrained expected-utility reasoning, compare concrete mechanisms with Hermes Agent, Pi, Codex, and Claude Code, and report implementation and regression-test evidence. The current evidence establishes executable contracts, not performance advantages, repair accuracy, or production recovery. The source code is open source under the MIT license at https://github.com/mz24cn/agents.

papers.title: Think2Listen: Evidence-Centric Learning For Agentic Audio Understanding With LALMS
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large audio-language models (LALMs) have broadened audio understanding across speech, sound, and music, with tool-based agents further supporting these tasks by invoking predefined audio tools. However, a persistent gap remains between perceiving acoustic content and using it as evidence for reasoning: recognizing what is audible does not ensure that a model can identify which cues resolve an uncertain decision. To bridge this gap, we propose Think2Listen, an evidence-centric learning framework for agentic audio understanding. Guided by evidence before commitment, Think2Listen couples iterative reasoning with a targeted LALM interaction to actively seek acoustic cues that distinguish competing hypotheses and revise candidate judgments based on the observations returned. It learns what to ask, how to use evidence, and when to stop, using observation-induced changes in candidate-state to inform training credit. Extensive evaluations on two benchmarks spanning seven audio categories demonstrate that Think2Listen achieves (I) enhanced multi-step audio reasoning, with gains in overall accuracy of 5.08%--17.67% over competing audio agents; and (II) improved audio understanding and reasoning across speech, sound, and music, boosting overall accuracy by 2.29%--13.10% over the corresponding baselines. The source code is available at https://github.com/JinWang79/Think2Listen.

papers.title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
papers.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text. A deterministic compiler turns each tool's schema and the request into multiple-choice questions whose options come from the request and the schema, then a one-pass decision model answers them. On 1,952 requests to 157 biomedical tools, the best System 1 agent chose the right tool, or correctly declined, for 97.0% of requests, significantly ahead of all 18 local LLM-agent settings (best 95.2%). The System 1 agent filled 97.0% of 6,056 stated argument values. No System 1 call contained invented content, against 5.5-19.7% of LLM calls. The System 1 Agents framework is freely available as open-source software at https://github.com/eltzanis/SystemOneAgents.

papers.title: GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry
papers.abstract: LLM agents answer closed-form questions over a tabular dataframe by writing and executing Python, almost always as a single rollout: one interpretation, one script, one result, accepted without comparison. The few pipelines that produce several candidates reconcile them by answer-agreement voting, which needs a single comparable scalar and always returns one, even when every candidate is wrong. We present GRACE (Generative, Ranked, Adaptive Code Ensemble), a production-oriented pipeline that instead runs parallel best-of-N selection specialised to dataframe code. N agents run concurrently under a strict, machine-checkable output contract, diversified by persona hints, per-retry rotation, and a two-regime temperature schedule. Rather than vote, GRACE judges the executed artefacts: a pairwise tournament pre-filters the pool and a domain-specialised guardrail either selects the best candidate or, when none is defensible, rejects the whole pool and abstains with a diagnosis (an option voting structurally lacks), which in turn drives an adaptive retry with per-agent feedback. On InfiAgent-DABench (DAEval, M = 246), using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as the backbone, GRACE raises answer match from 39% for a single-rollout baseline to 71% (+32 pp, 1.8x), recovering 53% of previously wrong answers. On the same DAEval task, the smaller dense Qwen3.5-9B lifts answer match from 38% to 63% (+25 pp, 1.7x). A controlled 3 x 3 study that sweeps the number of parallel agents against the retry budget finds, on the 35B backbone, the two levers largely substitutable: once either one is generous, the other adds little, identifying a cheap operating point for deployment. The same directional pattern replicates on the independent DataBench benchmark, again on the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone, where answer match rises by 15 percentage points (from 70% to 85%) across 400 sampled questions.

papers.title: MemDoctor: Stage-wise Error Attribution and Repair for MLLM Agent Memory
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) now assist users across sessions of images and text, carried by an external memory of what was said and shown. When such an assistant answers wrongly, the failure usually began earlier, in how a record was written, updated or retrieved, and the answer alone does not say where. We formalize multimodal memory as four stages, Write, Update, Retrieve and Answer, and define nine error types across them. A stage-resolved analysis on Mem-Gallery traces most failures to a source stage, and most of those lie before the answer. Injecting known errors against fact-preserving control edits, we then follow each tainted record downstream. Early errors survive to the answer as apparent evidence, and hurt most when no other record holds the fact. A diagnosis that trusts the quoted evidence therefore blames the stage where the error surfaces, not the one where it began. We propose MemDoctor, in which the MLLM that built the memory diagnoses its own failures. It traces each needed fact backward through the four stages, accepts a diagnosis only when the cited evidence is found in memory, and repairs that stage before answering again. On a 4B backbone, MemDoctor improves accuracy on both Mem-Gallery and MemLens, outperforming all evaluated 8B baselines, and the same loop also improves MuRAG and A-Mem.

papers.title: CuRSE-Bench: A Benchmark for Probing Cultural Blind Spots in Text-to-Image Safety Evaluation
papers.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) safety evaluation typically assigns each prompt or image a single culture-blind harm label, so content that is harmful only within a particular culture can pass as benign. We introduce CultureCraft, an agentic framework that constructs T2I prompts that appear benign under a general-purpose rubric yet carry a latent harmful meaning in a target culture, and use it to build CuRSE-Bench: 10,709 culture-specific prompts and 2,648 culture-general controls over six regions and ten harm axes, each drawn from a predefined knowledge base of documented harm vectors and traceable to at least two independent sources. Scoring every prompt under six region persona judges and a paired culture-blind judge, we find that the culture-blind judge under-rates culture-specific latent harm while matching the persona judges on the controls. Each persona judge, in turn, chiefly decodes its own region's latent harm under our instrument: a selective cultural blind spot that persists in deployed moderators.

papers.title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits
papers.abstract: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. We introduce ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Controlled walkthroughs define visits by physical room entry and deliberately include same-type room distractors and cross-session object changes. Our evaluation of 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks reveals substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated zero-shot model achieves 50.5% overall accuracy and 52.2% on a 450-question subset, compared with 90.1% for human annotators. The evaluated agentic frameworks offer no overall improvement over direct inference with the same base model. Analysis of agent execution traces reveals evidence omissions and incorrect cross-visit room associations as major failure modes, suggesting that iterative evidence seeking alone does not ensure consistent spatial memory. Further analyses expose a gap between recognizing familiar rooms and identifying the correct visited room, while annotation-guided sampling highlights the importance of preserving intervening visits and transitions. We also provide RS-30K, a separate training dataset from synthetic sources with no template, scene, route, or video overlap with the benchmark. Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B raises overall accuracy from 35.5% to 60.4%, with the largest gains in association and improvements extending to real-life scenes.

papers.title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
papers.abstract: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for iterative search and verification. Using Gemini 3.8 Flash for both planning and perception, VideoNexus achieves 88.6% accuracy on full LVBench, exceeding same-backbone static ingestion and built-in agentic processing by 3.6 and 1.1 points, respectively, at 44% of the latter's measured API cost. A paired LVBench subset ablation shows lower planner input and higher accuracy. With Kimi K3 as the shared backbone, VideoNexus improves over the official Video-GAIA ReAct harness by 8.5 points in our evaluation. These results support compact evidence exchange for combining detailed observation with efficient planning and reasoning.

papers.title: VIVID: A Visual Harness for Agentic Video Editing
papers.abstract: Video editing requires agents to make editing decisions grounded in audiovisual observations and precise temporal localization, and to evaluate their effects in rendered outputs. General-purpose coding agents possess strong comprehension, reasoning, and code execution capabilities, while media interaction and evidence management mechanisms tailored to video tasks can further unlock their editing potential. We introduce VIVID, a visual harness that supports multiple native coding agents in video post-production without additional model training. VIVID provides tools for on-demand video inspection, audio analysis, and transcription, and preserves observations alongside their corresponding media versions and temporal coordinates. Agents can actively retrieve these observations as they reason, perform edits using their native coding and shell tools, and inspect rendered outputs to guide subsequent revisions. On AgenticVBench, comprising 100 tasks across Assembly, Repair, Sequencing, and Repurpose, Codex with VIVID achieves an average score of 58.6%, an improvement of 20.2 percentage points over native Codex. The same harness also integrates with Claude Code and OpenCode, achieving average scores of 55.1% and 37.1%, respectively, both substantially exceeding their native baselines. These results highlight VIVID's potential as a reusable visual harness for extending the capabilities of general-purpose coding agents to video editing.

papers.title: EgoLink: Egocentric Language-Vision Interactive Network Knowledge Challenge Summary
papers.abstract: The EgoLink Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026 benchmarks egocentric multimodal intelligence linking first-person perception, social reasoning, and interactive action. Unlike benchmarks centered on visible objects and activities, EgoLink evaluates whether models can interpret emotional and social cues, resolve visually grounded references, and convert user requests into verified tool-mediated actions. Its two tracks cover social reasoning in egocentric video and interactive agents that complete service tasks through dialogue, tool use, and closed-loop execution. Together, they test whether perception, reasoning, and decision-making remain coupled under both offline question answering and state-changing interaction. We highlight a multi-stage Track 1 data pipeline for multiple-choice question (MCQ) generation, chain-of-thought generation, automatic quality grading, and video-contribution filtering. We summarize the task design, evaluation metrics, rules, leaderboards, and representative solutions. The benchmark combines objective answer scoring with process- and result-based evaluation, enabling analysis of both final correctness and execution quality. The best Track 1 system achieved 0.9263 accuracy, while the best Track 2 system achieved 0.844 joint success and 0.916 micro accuracy. Participant reports reveal a shared principle: strong systems make intermediate evidence explicit through candidate verification, option-robust reasoning, scenario-aware planning, tool canonicalization, and state-aware correction before answering or acting. These findings highlight the importance of process verification and evidence-grounded reasoning for reliable egocentric multimodal intelligence.

papers.abstract: Biomolecular foundation models predict the structures of proteins and their complexes accurately, and large language models (LLMs) reason in natural language, but the two remain separate: the abilities of the former are not part of a general-purpose LLM, and the reasoning of the latter does not enter a structure prediction. Calpha aims at one general model that folds proteins and complexes, understands protein sequence and structure, and lets its language reasoning influence the structures it predicts. This report covers the first step, in which an LLM outputs single-chain protein structures. Qwen3.5-9B reads a sequence enriched with ESM2 residue features. It can respond in text or emit a token that invokes a pretrained SimpleFold structure head, which receives information about the protein only through Qwen's residue states. Under a fixed folding request, the head achieves mean TM-scores of 0.808 on the FoldBench-334 development set, 0.635 on CASP16 domains and 0.900 on a CAMEO-style PDB set. We compare these predictions with a baseline in which ESM2-3B encodes the sequence and a fine-tuned SimpleFold-3B head predicts the coordinates. The two systems also differ in trainable weights, training duration and crop length. For chains of 100--299 residues, all three paired confidence intervals include zero. At 300--600 residues, the mean differences are -0.044, -0.160 and -0.025, respectively. In a separate test, four English request types triggered folding on every evaluated example. Protein training reduced accuracy on a 350-item MMLU-Pro subset from 77.4% to 70.3%. An LLM can therefore output single-chain structures from its own states, with lower long-chain scores in the current comparisons and reduced accuracy on the evaluated MMLU-Pro subset. Complex prediction, structure understanding and the effect of language reasoning on the predicted coordinates remain future work.

papers.title: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control
papers.brief: 构建手控视频世界模型，用手部感知监督学习手物交互，并以因果流映射和区域感知分数蒸馏实现少步生成，配合轻量视频解码器降低推理开销。

papers.what_it_is: 构建手控视频世界模型，用手部感知监督学习手物交互，并以因果流映射和区域感知分数蒸馏实现少步生成，配合轻量视频解码器降低推理开销。

papers.abstract: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. To address these challenges, we introduce LynnReal-Hand, a hand-controlled video world model that unifies precise interaction modeling with efficient streaming generation. We curate 100K interaction clips spanning diverse real and synthetic environments and develop hand-aware supervision to improve fine-grained hand motions and object interactions. Building on this foundation, we learn a causal flow map for few-step generation and introduce region-aware score distillation that combines complementary video and image priors to refine interaction dynamics and visual appearance. To further reduce inference latency, we propose Ultra-Fast-VAE, a compact video decoder that preserves high reconstruction fidelity with substantially lower computational cost. Extensive evaluations on HandBench demonstrate superior hand-following accuracy and visual quality compared with existing approaches. Our full-sequence model achieves an FVD of 181.67 and a MANO Dice score of 93.02, while the three-step causal model maintains a MANO Dice score of 92.49. For real-time interaction, 540p streaming on a single H200 reaches 18.03 FPS with 741ms latency and an optimized peak GPU memory footprint of only 34.89GB. We will release the datasets, model weights, and the full training and inference code to support research on hand-controlled video world models.

papers.abstract: Coding agents can synthesize and optimize code-based policies from simulator feedback, allowing the resulting program to act with zero inference model calls. But for long horizon tasks, two challenges arise: local improvements can hurt final success and switching to a new objective requires another expensive synthesis run. We propose a framework that first develops competence by refining the policy through a feedback cascade, moving from episode returns to hierarchical goals and belief updates which can be scored densely from simulator. In the Craftax game, a partially observed and procedurally generated environment, refinements via episode level feedback stall at <1% final-level arrival, whereas with the feedback cascade the optimized policy reaches the final stage 50% of time (28% final boss defeats). Furthermore, to make this competence reusable towards new goals, we factor the previous controller into an environment interpreter $I$ (models, memory, skills) and a rule program $p_0$, and we show that coding agents can optimize a reusable goal compiler $C_θ$ that maps structured tasks $g$ into new rule programs $p_g$. Across five independent compiler searches trained only on short tasks, the resulting compilers successfully transfer zero-shot to longer tasks without any task-specific tuning nor inference-time LLM calls: continuation-scored feedback and a fixed machine with an editable program together turn a single-task competent policy into a reusable one. papers.title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality

恢复未示范相似难例的性能，不降低未见物体成功率
papers.why_notable: 少量人类示范可定向补足强化学习的顽固盲点，并迁移到未示范的相似难例，为机器人抓取提供高效纠错路径。
papers.abstract: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. A grasping policy that works directly on the point cloud from a depth sensor needs only the geometry the robot observes, so it applies to any new object. Offline grasp generators such as Contact-GraspNet work this way, but they rank grasps by learned plausibility rather than by whether the grasp actually lifts the object. Reinforcement learning (RL) can optimize for that directly and make a point-cloud grasping policy much better on average, yet it leaves specific grasps persistently unsolved. We present a human-in-the-loop failure loop that targets those grasps: situations an RL policy keeps failing are mined automatically, sent to a virtual-reality application where a person picks the object up with their own hands, and returned to training as two grasp points. The person contributes only where to grasp; the robot chooses its own approach. In simulation, RL raises success on unseen objects from 55% with Contact-GraspNet to 83%. Adding 58 human demonstrations nearly doubles success on the hard cases RL kept failing, from 24% to 45%, and recovers performance that RL alone loses on similar cases that were never demonstrated, without reducing success on unseen objects.

papers.title: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images
papers.brief: 构建由物理模拟器判定结果的二维场景基准，用微小几何变化形成成对样本，并设置四级提示，定位视觉语言模型预测连锁反应的失败环节。
papers.tldr: 静态图像连锁反应测试揭示，多模态模型难以自主算出决定物理结果的关键量。
papers.what_it_is: 构建由物理模拟器判定结果的二维场景基准，用微小几何变化形成成对样本，并设置四级提示，定位视觉语言模型预测连锁反应的失败环节。
key_points: DominoBench含854题、427组最小差异对，测试30个模型。
无提示时，前沿模型关键人物判断最高72%，成对全对最高34%。
给出决定性计算及所需量后，强模型准确率升至82%—92%。
papers.why_notable: 将流畅场景描述与可靠物理预测区分开，指出关键瓶颈在自主获取并计算决定性物理量，为现实世界规划模型提供针对性评测。
papers.abstract: Can a vision-language model look at a picture of a chain reaction and tell what will happen? Recent multimodal models describe scenes fluently and solve textbook physics problems, which suggests they should also predict how a scene of ramps, ledges, pendulums, seesaws and dominoes plays out once a ball is pushed. We tested this claim on 30 models from 10 families and reached a clear conclusion: unaided, no model predicts the outcome reliably. We built DominoBench, a benchmark of still images of 2D rigid-body scenes whose outcome a physics simulator computes. It holds 854 items in 427 minimal pairs, in which a change of one to three grid steps in one quantity decides whether one person survives, and every item comes with a four-rung hint ladder ending in the exact calculation that decides the outcome. Unaided, frontier models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI are right about the person whose fate flips in at most 72% of items and answer both twins of a pair correctly in at most 34%. Pointing at the deciding step helps little, and exact geometry given as text barely helps, yet once the deciding calculation and the quantities it needs, including speeds that a still image cannot show, are written out, the same models reach 82-92% on the deciding person, while small open-weight models stay near chance. Physical prediction from a still image therefore fails at the quantitative step: the strongest models use the deciding quantity when they are given it, but do not produce it on their own. For models that plan or act in the physical world, a fluent account of a scene is thus no evidence of a correct prediction: such models must find and compute the deciding quantity unprompted, and DominoBench tests whether they do.

papers.title: More Agents, More Samples, or More Thinking? Untangling Coordination, Ensembling, and Test-Time Compute in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.brief: 研究汇总九项实证评估，用六维资源向量和四类基线拆分协作、采样与推理计算的贡献，并通过多层随机效应模型检验多智能体的净收益。
papers.tldr: 综合九项评估发现，多智能体在匹配采样数或资源预算后通常不优于基线。
papers.what_it_is: 研究汇总九项实证评估，用六维资源向量和四类基线拆分协作、采样与推理计算的贡献，并通过多层随机效应模型检验多智能体的净收益。
key_points: 汇总9项评估，覆盖516种多智能体配置
匹配采样数或资源预算后，准确率平均差为-0.042
74%的可比对照中，多智能体准确率不高于基线
papers.why_notable: 它将多智能体协作收益与额外采样、计算投入区分开，为公平评测提供依据，也提示应关注证据分工、外部验证和模型错误多样性。
papers.abstract: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. This practice confounds coordination with sample multiplicity and inference compute. We synthesize nine primary empirical evaluations comprising 516 unique multi-agent configurations organized along a resource vector R with six dimensions and a baseline ladder with four categories. Against baselines with a single pass (Category A), multi-agent accuracy differences are negative overall and near zero when omitting the largest contributing study. When evaluated against baselines matched on sample count (Category B) or resource budget (Category C), multi-agent systems average -0.042 in accuracy, and multilevel random effects modeling on the log odds scale remains negative across sensitivity checks. Multi-agent accuracy equals or falls below the baseline in 74% of these comparable contrasts, and study means are nonpositive in almost all evaluated studies. Across studies reporting both baselines, moving from a greedy pass to a sampled baseline shifts accuracy differences by -0.038 on average. Because communication adds no information when agents share identical evidence, positive returns require partitioned evidence, external verification, or error diversity across models. We provide a reviewer checklist and accounting utilities.

papers.title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
papers.brief: LoopFill是无需训练的循环模型推测解码算法，将后缀多词草稿与浅循环预测合入同一草稿树，批量处理不同循环深度的候选，再以完整深度验证。
papers.tldr: 融合后缀多词草稿与浅层预测，让循环语言模型并行解码提速且保持输出分布。
papers.what_it_is: LoopFill是无需训练的循环模型推测解码算法，将后缀多词草稿与浅循环预测合入同一草稿树，批量处理不同循环深度的候选，再以完整深度验证。
key_points: 后缀查找直接扩展浅层预测，多词同时进入流水线
七项基准平均加速：Ouro为5.85倍，Huginn为5.13倍
较LoopAhead分别多提速40%和25%
papers.why_notable: 它缓解循环模型逐词多次串行计算的延迟，无需额外训练且保持自回归输出分布，为参数高效模型提供更实用的推理路径。
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by repeatedly applying the same Transformer layers. During autoregressive decoding, however, generating each token requires several sequential passes through these layers, leading to high decoding latency. Pipelined self-speculative methods use shallow-loop predictions to process tokens at different loops in the same batch, but each token must reach the drafting depth before the next can enter the pipeline. We introduce LoopFill, a training-free speculative decoding algorithm for looped LLM that combines multi-token suffix drafts with shallow-loop predictions in a single draft tree. Both drafters contribute to one tree, so a suffix lookup can immediately extend a shallow prediction and several future tokens can enter the pipeline together. The shared block computes the highest-scoring draft candidates at different loop depths in one batch, and full-depth verification preserves the model's autoregressive output distribution. Across seven benchmarks, LoopFill's average speedup over greedy autoregressive decoding is $5.85\times$ on Ouro-2.6B and $5.13\times$ on Huginn-3.5B. The speedups exceed those of LoopAhead, the strongest baseline, by \(40\%\) on Ouro-2.6B and \(25\%\) on Huginn-3.5B.

papers.title: When Expert Disagreement Hurts: Prestige and Selectivity in LLM Decision Revision
papers.brief: 研究用受控两轮审计固定问题、证据与初始答案，仅改变中立反思、匿名异议或专家异议情境，区分纠正错误与放弃正确答案。
papers.tldr: 专家异议可能让模型放弃正确答案，修订是否有效取决于纠错选择性。
papers.what_it_is: 研究用受控两轮审计固定问题、证据与初始答案，仅改变中立反思、匿名异议或专家异议情境，区分纠正错误与放弃正确答案。
key_points: 覆盖5个模型、1989项医学、科学与法律决策
初始准确率90%时，纠错率须超过改错率9倍
专家异议下无模型达到选择性门槛，准确率最多降16.1个百分点
papers.why_notable: 将答案反转拆成纠错与改错，揭示专家标签带来的威望偏差；为模型修订流程提供比反转次数更可靠的配对条件指标。
papers.abstract: When language models revise a decision after another agent disagrees, neither reversal counts nor final accuracy shows whether they are fixing mistakes or abandoning correct answers.
